pk.context: 5 mg/kg intravenous, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: clear to opalescent solution in a single-dose vial

clues.kinetics: It is expected to be metabolized into small peptides by catabolic pathways, and hydroxyurea had no clinically meaningful effect on its pharmacokinetics.
clues.substance: Made by recombinant DNA technology in Chinese hamster ovary cells, with a theoretical molecular weight of about 146 kDa. Supplied as a sterile, preservative-free solution.
clues.product: Approved under BLA 761128 as a single-dose vial of 100 mg per 10 mL, given at weeks 0 and 2 and then every 4 weeks.
clues.safety: No boxed warning and no contraindications. Arthralgia and nausea are among the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Reducing the frequency of vaso-occlusive crises in patients aged 16 years and older with sickle cell disease.
clues.mechanism: Binds P-selectin and blocks its interactions with ligands such as PSGL-1, and can break apart preformed P-selectin/PSGL-1 complexes.

tell: A humanized IgG2 kappa antibody that can also break apart preformed P-selectin/PSGL-1 complexes.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: Administer 5 mg/kg by intravenous infusion over a period of 30 minutes on Week 0
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: terminal elimination half-life (t 1/2 ) of crizanlizumab-tmca was 10.6 (20.5%) days
